meta.title: Thank You from Palm Lake
meta.textType: functional: two emails on one topic, for two readers

paragraphs: On Monday, March twenty-ninth, Lily sat at her desk at home. It was the second week of the school holiday, and Pip lay on the floor at her feet. Teacher Kim sent her a note with two emails. The note said, "Lily, please read both." Lily opened the two emails side by side on her laptop. The left one was from Ms. Ong to Teacher Kim, and the right one was from Grace to Lily. She read the left one first.

Dear Teacher Kim, thank you for the video call on Tuesday, March sixteenth. The children liked it very much. I want to tell you that the sound problem was in our school, not in your laptop. Please thank the Explorers for their questions. Please visit our class page online, because our pupils put their drawings there. In the future, the pen pals will write to each other again. Best wishes, Ms. Ong.

Dear Lily, thank you for the video call. You looked at your paper, so I think that you had a question. Was it about my violin? I surf the web daily to find new comics. In June, I will take a swimming course, and I need a new bathing suit. My brother plays cricket and rugby, and his team has training on Saturdays. He tells me that rugby is better than cricket. How is Pip? Please write to me soon. Best wishes, Grace.

The two emails were about the same call, but they were for two readers. Ms. Ong wrote to a teacher, so her email was short and polite. Grace wrote to a friend, so her email was long and friendly. Lily thought, "A pupil writes to a teacher in one way and to a friend in another way." She looked at the question about the violin and smiled. "Grace saw me look at my paper," she said to Pip. Pip did not answer, and he closed his eyes.

Lily remembered May's words in the library, "Write it in your email." She clicked on "Reply" under Grace's email. Lily typed her own reply with a smile. Lily typed, "Yes, and how long do you practice every day?" Pip lifted his head and looked at the screen. Lily pressed the button to send it. Then she waited for Grace's answer.
text.summary: Teacher Kim sends Lily two emails about the video call. One is a short email from Ms. Ong to Teacher Kim, and one is a friendly email from Grace to Lily. Lily replies to Grace with her question about the violin.
